why is everyone quote posting the same sentence?? where did this start
grounding: The focused post by @crobertcargill.bsky.social (C. Robert Cargill) is one link in a quote chain 27 posts deep. Every post repeats the text 'Bluesky is a town and we all have a job here. What is yours?' and each person adds their own answer as a GIF, image or video. It is a chain game, not an argument. The script's default follows 20 posts back; with a higher --max-depth the chain reaches @doyleinstitute.bsky.social on 2026-11-19 16:07 UTC, whose post quotes a post that has since been deleted, so the true origin cannot be seen. A good answer explains the game, says how far back it could trace and that the first post is gone, and does not invent an originator.

what scandal are they all talking about? i feel like im missing the start of this
grounding: The tapped post by Mark Copelovitch ('There are no conservatives left in the current Republican Party…') is 5th in a quote chain: BeijingPalmer ('oh so now this really is the biggest national security scandal in American history', 14:27 UTC) → Elizabeth N. Saunders agrees → Radley Balko says the president pressured a private company to reinstall a disgraced CEO 'caught in a ChiCom honey trap' → Raven Onthill asks where the conservatives are → Copelovitch. None of the posts names the company; it is the Nvidia / Jensen Huang story trending the same day ('Nvidia rehires Huang', 'Alice Huang espionage allegations'). A good answer walks the chain back, attributes each line to its author, connects it to the trending story with a source, and marks the commentators' characterizations (such as 'honey trap') as their claims, not established fact.

grounding: Jamelle Bouie's post ('yes, the reason why trump will never remove hegseth is that hegseth will unhesitatingly give the order to shoot americans') is 4th in a chain: Isaac Chotiner posts his New Yorker interview 'The Former Trump Official Who Thinks Trump's Staff Has Let Him Down' → LOLGOP says the interviewee 'thinks Trump doesn't look under the hood, especially with Hegseth' and disagrees → Andy Craig argues Hegseth was appointed for his record seeking pardons for war criminals → Bouie agrees with Craig. So the 'doesn't look under the hood' view belongs to the interviewed former official, as paraphrased by LOLGOP; Bouie holds the opposite view. The New Yorker page may be paywalled. A good answer says no, corrects the attribution, and names the original as Chotiner's interview.
